recipes.name: Broken Glass Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 ounce) package lime flavored Jell-O® mix
1 (3 ounce) package orange flavored Jell-O® mix

steps.text: Place lime, orange, and strawberry gelatin mixes into 3 separate 9x9-inch glass dishes.
Pour 1 cup boiling water into each flavor of gelatin mix; stir the gelatin until dissolved.
Pour 1 cup cold water into each flavor of gelatin, stir to combine, and refrigerate the 3 flavors of gelatin until set, at least 4 hours.

Heat pineapple juice in a saucepan until hot but not simmering. Stir unflavored gelatin into pineapple juice until dissolved. Refrigerate pineapple juice mixture until cool and thickened, about 30 minutes. Stir occasionally.

Mix graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and brown sugar together in a bowl. Set 1 cup of crumb mixture aside for garnish. Press remaining 2 cups crumb mixture into the bottom of a 9x13-inch cake pan to make a crust.

Pour cream into a large metal mixing bowl and beat with an electric mixer until the cream is fluffy and forms soft peaks, about 3 minutes. Slowly beat sugar into whipped cream, 1 or 2 tablespoons at a time; beat in vanilla extract.
Cut the different flavors of gelatin into cubes. Use a thin spatula to lift the cubes away from the bottom of the dish and loosen them.
Very gently fold the thickened pineapple juice and gelatin cubes into the whipped cream mixture until thoroughly combined. Spoon into the graham cracker crust.
Sprinkle the cake with reserved graham cracker crumb mixture.
Refrigerate until set, at least 3 hours to overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Broken Glass Cake
raw_recipe.description: This broken glass cake is easy to make with 3 different colors of gelatin and whipped cream in a graham cracker crust for a fun retro dessert.

video.description: Try this creamy, family-friendly dessert that perfectly balances out a heavy dinner! In this video, Nicole shows you how to make broken glass cake using three different flavors of jello. This no-bake cake mixes together a pineapple juice cream filling with “stained glass shards” of jello to create a colorful and fruity flavored dish. Poured onto a sweet graham cracker crust and chilled overnight, broken glass cake is decadent and easy-to-make!

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe many times over the years. It can also be sugarfree using diabetic jellos. I really do not know why it is always described as a childrens dessert because it is very much appreciated by adults and a wonderful addition to Xmas desserts.

Growing up, over 50 years ago, this was my all-time favorite. We called this "Broken Glass Torte". It was made with a graham cracker crust in a springform pan. I omitted the graham cracker topping and only used 1/2 cup of cold water in each flavor. This was a hit in the 1960s, and it is still a hit today. A golden oldie!
This is a great recipe but substitute the graham crackers for lady fingers. It is a very light dessert and the presentation is very colorful

As others have said, this is not just for kids! This is the best version of this simple dessert - it uses real whipped cream, pineapple juice and unflavoured gelatin to bind the gelatin cubes. The only modification I made was to make gelatin with 3/4 cup of hot and cold water (that is using 75% of total water instead of 100%), so the gelatin cubes would be firmer, less likely to fall apart when mixed with cream mixture. I was pleased this was not coyingly sweet - a nice balanced favour. I know it’s just a gelatin dessert , but this is worth making. We loved this decades ago as kids, and it sure is nice to resurrect such a good tasting version for the “kiddies” in all of us

The only thing wrong is the jello. 
Use 1 cup hot water and 1/2 cup cold.
You will have better results when you combined all.
Jello will stay together.

I only saved 3/4 cup of the crumb mix for the topping and I added a fourth gelatin
Lemon, Strawberry, Berry Berry, and Concord Grape.
I had this every year for Christmas (do to it's celebratory colors) and at Thanksgiving (due to its easy and not so filling/rich tastes and flavors)
This is a fabulous dish that everyone should try

Jello made with only 1 1/2 cups of liquid keep a nicer shape. I decided to top mine with rainbow coloured coconut as it adds nicely to the flavour. I had never thought to put it on top of graham crust so two thumbs up for that suggestion its in the fridge now cant wait for dessert tonight:D
Ive had this recipe for over 40 years but it calls for Cool Whip instead of the heavy cream. Im interested to combine both recipes to add the brown sugar and vanilla and see how it turns out!
I make it add cream cheese to it and a bit more powdered sugar I also add 2 more colors of jello to it as well adding the cream cheese it just goes with the pineapple juice flavoring

This recipe was a must for my sister (rip). It was my sister's signature dessert. She was asked to make this for every family event. Did not make a graham cracker topping. Was not needed. But, instead of a 9x13 pan, it was made in a mold, when she needed to unmold it, placed bottom of mold into warm water until it was able to unmold onto a plate. Placed a plate on open side of mold, turned it over to unmold onto the plate. Spectacular! Nobody has attempted to make it.

I am so happy to come across this recipe! My mother used to make this or very similar) for church suppers in the 60's/70's, before there was blue jello. But she concocted her own blue jello to add. Our church had gorgeous stained glass windows, which is maybe why everyone I knew called this "stained glass" salad, pudding, or cake, depending on how it was served.
When I was a kid my mother made this in an Angel food tin, that was 60 years ago, I like this way of using a 9x13 sheet pan. I switched graham wafers out for chocolate cookie crumbs.

Love this stuff!! Growing up my grandmother made this every Christmas. We called it "Cracked Glass Cake". This really tastes like hers did. I wish I would have asked her for the recipe when I had the chance.
This is the real broken glass cake recipe it has real cream in it as supposed to be
I will make this repeatedly! I had this recipe for years and then misplaced it. So happy to find it again!
I made this but found the Jello had way too much water as when I went to fold it into the whip cream part it fell apart and looks awful. I think it will taste okay thought.
We always called this prizm cake.
In 2010, I tried an earlier AR version of this recipe. VERY GOOD. Be sure to give the final product plenty of time to completely set up.
